label: prf:prolonged-periods-fixed-depth
title: Proof that a fixed-depth recurrence for the prolonged periods exists
html:
Proof. Proof that a fixed-depth recurrence for the prolonged periods exists

Let V be the Gauss--Manin period space of the Seiberg--Witten family over Bring's surface — the de Rham cohomology of the family, a finitely generated free R-module of rank r = \dim V \leq 2g = 8. Let M : V \to V be the jet-prolongation operator (prop:mi-sw-abelianisation), v_0 \in V the base period vector, and \varphi : V \to R the period functional, so a_D^{(n)} = \varphi(M^n v_0).

Cayley--Hamilton. Because V is finite-rank, M satisfies its characteristic polynomial: there is d \leq r and coefficients c_0,\dots,c_{d-1} \in R with M^d = \sum_{j<d} c_j\,M^j.

Operator recurrence. For any n, using M^{n+d} = M^n\!\cdot M^d, the Cayley--Hamilton relation, and distributivity of multiplication over the finite sum,

M^{n+d} = M^n\!\cdot\!\Big(\sum_{j<d} c_j M^j\Big)
        = \sum_{j<d} c_j\,(M^n\!\cdot M^j)
        = \sum_{j<d} c_j\,M^{n+j},

where the middle step is mul_smul_comm (scalars commute past the operator product) and the last is M^n\!\cdot M^j = M^{n+j}.

Period recurrence. Applying the linear functional T \mapsto \varphi(T v_0) to both sides and using its additivity and R-homogeneity (map_sum, map_smul),

a_D^{(n+d)} = \sum_{j<d} c_j\,a_D^{(n+j)},

a depth-d linear recurrence with n-independent kernel c. Hence a fixed-depth recurrence on the prolonged periods exists, with depth bounded by \mathrm{rank}\, V. Identifying d and c with the Bring Picard--Fuchs operator is the remaining (identification) half of conj:qdifference-kernel-prolongation-symbol. \qquad\blacksquare
